say.en: Most compounds of sodium are white, but transition-metal compounds come in every colour, many are attracted by a magnet, and many speed up industrial reactions. All three come from unpaired d electrons. In this lesson: Calculate spin-only magnetic moments.
Explain the colour of transition-metal ions.
Describe catalytic behaviour, interstitial compounds and alloys.

body.en: A substance with unpaired electrons is paramagnetic: it is attracted into a *magnetic* field. One with all electrons paired is diamagnetic. For 3d ions the moment comes almost entirely from electron spin, so the spin-only formula gives it from the number of unpaired electrons, n. The unit is the Bohr magneton (BM).
body.kn: ಜೋಡಿಯಾಗದ ಇಲೆಕ್ಟ್ರಾನುಗಳಿರುವ ವಸ್ತು ಅನುಕಾಂತೀಯ; ಎಲ್ಲ ಇಲೆಕ್ಟ್ರಾನುಗಳು ಜೋಡಿಯಾಗಿದ್ದರೆ ಪ್ರತಿಕಾಂತೀಯ. ಸ್ಪಿನ್-ಮಾತ್ರ ಕಾಂತೀಯ ಭ್ರಾಮಕ μ = √(n(n+2)) BM.

title.en: On the board: magnetism and colour

say.en: Unpaired electrons make an ion paramagnetic. The spin-only moment is root n into n plus 2 Bohr magnetons.
One unpaired electron gives 1.73, three give 3.87, five give 5.92. Iron two plus, d six, has four unpaired: 4.90.
In a complex the d orbitals split. An electron jumps up by absorbing one colour of light; we see the complementary colour.
Ti three plus, d one, is purple; Cu two plus, d nine, is blue. d zero and d ten ions have no d–d jump, so they are colourless.
Transition metals are good catalysts because of variable oxidation states and large surfaces. Similar radii let them form alloys.
Small atoms such as carbon, nitrogen and hydrogen fit into the metal lattice: interstitial compounds, hard and high-melting.

title.en: Magnetic moment and colour of 3d ions

narration.en: Choose an ion. Its unpaired 3d electrons give a spin-only magnetic moment μ = √(n(n + 2)) BM, so the more unpaired electrons, the stronger the pull of a magnet. Ions with a partly filled 3d set absorb visible light (d–d transitions) and are coloured; d⁰ and d¹⁰ ions are colourless.
narration.kn: ಅಯಾನು ಆರಿಸಿ. ಜೋಡಿಯಾಗದ 3d ಇಲೆಕ್ಟ್ರಾನ್‌ಗಳು μ = √(n(n + 2)) BM ಕೊಡುತ್ತವೆ. ಭಾಗಶಃ ತುಂಬಿದ 3d ಇರುವ ಅಯಾನುಗಳು ಗೋಚರ ಬೆಳಕು ಹೀರಿ ಬಣ್ಣ ಹೊಂದಿರುತ್ತವೆ; d⁰, d¹⁰ ಬಣ್ಣರಹಿತ.

title.en: Colour, catalysis, interstitial compounds and alloys

body.en: In a complex or a hydrated ion, the d orbitals split into two energy levels. An electron absorbs visible light to jump to the upper level (a d–d transition), and we see the complementary colour: [Ti(H₂O)₆]³⁺ is violet, [Cu(H₂O)₆]²⁺ blue. d⁰ and d¹⁰ ions (Sc³⁺, Ti⁴⁺, Zn²⁺, Cu⁺) are colourless. Transition metals are good catalysts because they show variable oxidation states and offer surfaces for adsorption: V₂O₅ (Contact process), Fe (Haber process), Ni (hydrogenation); Fe³⁺ catalyses the reaction of I⁻ with S₂O₈²⁻. Small atoms such as H, C and N fit into their lattices to give hard, high-melting, inert *interstitial compounds*. Similar atomic radii let them form alloys: brass (Cu–Zn), bronze (Cu–Sn), steels.
body.kn: d–d ಸಂಕ್ರಮಣದಿಂದ ಸಂಕ್ರಮಣ ಲೋಹ ಅಯಾನುಗಳು ಬಣ್ಣ ಹೊಂದಿವೆ; d⁰ ಮತ್ತು d¹⁰ ಅಯಾನುಗಳು ಬಣ್ಣರಹಿತ. ಬದಲಾಗುವ ಆಕ್ಸಿಡೀಕರಣ ಸ್ಥಿತಿಗಳಿಂದ ಅವು ಉತ್ತಮ ವೇಗವರ್ಧಕಗಳು. ಅವು ಅಂತರಾಳೀಯ ಸಂಯುಕ್ತಗಳು ಮತ್ತು ಮಿಶ್ರಲೋಹಗಳನ್ನು ರೂಪಿಸುತ್ತವೆ.

aim.en: To verify the Beer–Lambert law for potassium permanganate and find the concentration of an unknown solution. problem.en: Calculate the spin-only magnetic moment of Fe²⁺ (Z of Fe = 26).

steps.en: Fe²⁺ = [Ar] 3d⁶: five d orbitals hold 6 electrons, so one pair and 4 unpaired electrons: n = 4.

narration.en: Let us solve this together. Calculate the spin-only magnetic moment of Fe²⁺ (Z of Fe = 26).

say.en: Let us solve this together. Calculate the spin-only magnetic moment of Fe squared⁺ Z of Fe equals 26.
Fe squared⁺ = [Ar] 3d to the power 6: five d orbitals hold 6 electrons, so one pair and 4 unpaired electrons: n equals 4.
micro equals the square root of 4 times 6 equals the square root of 24.
micro equals 4.90 BM.
So the answer is 4.90 BM.

problem.en: A divalent 3d ion has a spin-only moment of 3.87 BM. How many unpaired electrons does it have, and which ion could it be?

steps.en: A d³ ion with charge +2: V²⁺ (V is 3d³ 4s², so V²⁺ is 3d³). (A d⁷ ion such as Co²⁺, high spin, also has 3 unpaired electrons.)

say.en: Let us solve this together. A divalent 3d ion has a spin-only moment of 3.87 BM. How many unpaired electrons does it have, and which ion could it be?
the square root of (nn plus 2) equals 3.87 gives nn plus 2 equals 15 gives n equals 3.
A d cubed ion with charge plus 2: V squared⁺ (V is 3d cubed 4 square seconds, so V squared⁺ is 3d cubed). (A d to the power 7 ion such as Co squared⁺, high spin, also has 3 unpaired electrons.).
So the answer is n equals 3, e.g. V squared⁺ or Co squared⁺.

narration.en: Recap. Spin-only moment μ = √(n(n+2)) BM; n = unpaired electrons. Colour comes from d–d transitions; d⁰ and d¹⁰ ions are colourless. Catalysts: V₂O₅ (Contact), Fe (Haber), Ni (hydrogenation). Interstitial compounds are hard, high-melting and inert; similar radii allow alloys.
narration.kn: ಪುನರಾವರ್ತನೆ. ಸ್ಪಿನ್-ಮಾತ್ರ ಭ್ರಾಮಕ μ = √(n(n+2)) BM. ಬಣ್ಣ d–d ಸಂಕ್ರಮಣದಿಂದ; d⁰, d¹⁰ ಬಣ್ಣರಹಿತ. ವೇಗವರ್ಧಕಗಳು: V₂O₅, Fe, Ni. ಅಂತರಾಳೀಯ ಸಂಯುಕ್ತಗಳು ಗಟ್ಟಿ, ಜಡ; ಸಮಾನ ಗಾತ್ರದಿಂದ ಮಿಶ್ರಲೋಹಗಳು.

say.en: Let us recall the key ideas. Spin-only moment micro equals the square root of (nn plus 2) BM; n equals unpaired electrons.
say.kn: ಮುಖ್ಯ ಅಂಶಗಳನ್ನು ನೆನಪಿಸಿಕೊಳ್ಳೋಣ. ಸ್ಪಿನ್-ಮಾತ್ರ ಭ್ರಾಮಕ micro equals the square root of (nn plus 2) BM.

say.en: Colour comes from d-d transitions; d to the power 0 and d to the power 10 ions are colourless.
say.kn: ಬಣ್ಣ d-d ಸಂಕ್ರಮಣದಿಂದ; d to the power 0, d to the power 10 ಬಣ್ಣರಹಿತ.

say.en: Catalysts: V 2O 5 Contact, Fe Haber, Ni hydrogenation.
Interstitial compounds are hard, high-melting and inert; similar radii allow alloys.
say.kn: ಅಂತರಾಳೀಯ ಸಂಯುಕ್ತಗಳು ಗಟ್ಟಿ, ಜಡ; ಸಮಾನ ಗಾತ್ರದಿಂದ ಮಿಶ್ರಲೋಹಗಳು.
